title: Cross-region failover spike: tail-latency degradation, SLO breach and remediation plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a traffic spike on 2026-02-27 we triggered a cross-region failover for eu-west when us-central degraded. The secondary region (eu-west) returned to service but showed persistent elevated P95/P99 tail latency for text-generation requests for ~42 minutes, causing an SLO miss for end-to-end latency and increased error budgets for several customers. This ticket captures incident findings, root-cause analysis, and a prioritized remediation/action tracker to reduce recurrence risk.
timeline: 2026-02-27T09:12Z - Alert: Global latency SLO alert fired (P99 generation > 750ms for 5m).
2026-02-27T09:16Z - Traffic routing controller initiated region failover: 60% of incoming traffic moved from us-central -> eu-west in staged steps.
2026-02-27T09:18Z - eu-west nodes accepted traffic but KV cache hit-rate dropped from 92%->18% as new prefixes were requested and cache was cold.
2026-02-27T09:22Z - Circuit breaker policy for model-serve pool in eu-west began tripping due to transient latency; fallback queues increased fan-out.
2026-02-27T09:24Z - Autoscaler started scaling worker GPUs, but node readiness and model warmup latency introduced a 6-8 minute ramp.
2026-02-27T09:30Z - Error rate rose (502/504s) as some worker pools hit memory pressure while handling KV-miss cold-start windows.
2026-02-27T09:54Z - Traffic gradually recovered to normal latencies after cache warmed and autoscaler completed scale-up. Incident duration ~42 minutes.
2026-03-01T13:00Z - Initial incident review completed; high-level notes and metrics posted to incident doc.
root_causes: Aggressive cross-region failover policy moved a large fraction of traffic before secondary region caches and worker pools were warm (routing policy tuned for fast failover, not warmup).

Protective circuit-breaker thresholds in eu-west were calibrated conservatively for single-region traffic and tripped under sudden fan-in from routed traffic, causing cascading retries and queue amplification.
KV prefix cache is region-local and not pre-populated on failover; cold cache led to repetitive model lookups and KV-store amplification under load.
Autoscaler vertical and model warmup path has a long tail: GPU nodes marked ready before model processes finished warming KV and tokenizer caches, creating a window of degraded throughput.
SLO alerting and runbook lacked a coordinated warming step for cross-region failover and gave insufficient guidance on partial-traffic ramping when cold caches are expected.
impact_metrics: SLO: generation end-to-end P99 breached target (target 500ms) — observed 980ms at peak.
Error budget consumed: 14% for affected accounts in eu-west over rolling hour.
Customer-visible errors: 0.9% request error rate spike (baseline 0.03%).
KV cache hit-rate dropped to 18% immediately after failover; returned to >90% after ~20-30 minutes of sustained traffic.
Autoscaler added 6 GPU nodes; model warmup added ~4-8 minutes of latency per new node.
action_items: (P0) Implement staged traffic ramp for cross-region failover: initially shift 10% every 30s with configurable warmup gates (owner: Lucas Moreno, due: 2026-03-18, estimate: 3).
(P0) Add a cache-warmup preflight during failover: fetch top N KV prefixes for active customers into secondary region before increasing traffic (owner: Meera Singh, due: 2026-03-20, estimate: 5).

(P1) Adjust circuit-breaker thresholds to incorporate expected cold-cache latency distributions; add adaptive backoff that considers cache hit-rate (owner: Rafael Ortega, due: 2026-03-26, estimate: 5).

(P1) Improve autoscaler/model-warmup readiness signal: expose explicit 'model-ready' metric once tokenizer/KV warmed to avoid premature readiness marking (owner: Priya Rao, due: 2026-03-22, estimate: 3).

(P2) Update runbooks and alerting playbooks to include 'pre-warm and stagger' steps for regional failover and include checklist items for verifying cache hit-rate before full traffic shift (owner: On-call team, due: 2026-03-15, estimate: 2).
(P2) Add synthetic traffic drills in staging to validate warmup gating and circuit-breaker behavior under cross-region failover scenarios (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-04-02, estimate: 8).
(P3) Long-term: evaluate geo-replication of frequently-accessed KV prefixes for high-traffic customers to reduce cold-start amplification (owner: Storage infra, due: 2026-06-01, estimate: 13).
